trackers.product_line: AppsFlyer's measurement SDK: attribution, analytics and fraud protection for app developers
data_collected: the Android advertising ID, by default
installs, app launches and the in-app events the developer chooses, such as purchases
taps on and views of the developer's ads
IP address, mapped to region or city
device details: model, operating system, CPU and battery, network, motion sensors and screen orientation
a user ID the developer sets, and in some cases a hashed email or phone number
trackers.monetization_model: AppsFlyer sells attribution, analytics and fraud-protection services to app developers. It says it processes app users' data only for the developer, doesn't sell it and isn't an ad network or data broker; it uses de-identified aggregates of that data for market research, benchmarks and marketing its own services (its documentation).

data_flows.purpose: Installs, app launches, your taps on the developer's ads and the in-app events it chooses, such as purchases, so the developer can measure its marketing and check for fraud
data_flows.wording: According to AppsFlyer's documentation (read 2026-10-08) and its help centre (updated 2026-10-01).

consequences.text: If the developer has connected ad networks or other partners, AppsFlyer passes them your advertising ID and the events the developer picks, for example through postbacks; AppsFlyer counts that as sharing. FinePrint can't see that setting.
consequences.wording: According to AppsFlyer's documentation (read 2026-10-08) and its help centre (updated 2026-10-01).
